title: Government unveils leasehold service charge reforms
summary:
The Government has published new regulations to reform leasehold service charges in England, with the first measures coming into force on 1st April 2027. The reforms will strengthen leaseholders' rights to receive detailed information about service charges and challenge costs they consider unfair.

The post Government unveils leasehold service charge reforms appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Cotswolds developer secures £1.3m overdraft facility
summary:
Alternative Bridging Corporation has provided a £1.3 million overdraft facility to a Cotswolds-based housebuilder experiencing cash flow pressure due to delays between property reservations and completed sales. The facility, structured at 55% loan-to-value, allows the developer to draw funds as needed rather than taking the full amount immediately.

title: Lender provides £900,000 bridge on listed properties
summary:
Precise Mortgages has completed a £900,000 bridging loan secured against two Grade II listed properties in London, enabling clients to purchase a retirement home in Sussex. The 12-month loan was arranged by broker Yomo Finance and completed 25 days after the initial offer.

title: Wealth manager calls for scrapping of mansion tax
summary:
The chief executive of deVere Group has called for the government to scrap the High Value Council Tax Surcharge before its implementation in April 2028. The tax will apply to homes in England valued above £2 million, affecting fewer than 1% of properties.

title: ClearScore launches free rent reporting to credit bureaus
summary:
ClearScore has launched a free rent payment reporting service that allows private sector tenants to add their rental payments to credit reports held by all three major credit bureaus in the UK. The service enables tenants to report payments to Experian, Equifax and TransUnion through the ClearScore app or website.

title: First-time buyer mortgage costs rise 41% in a decade
summary:
First-time buyers in the UK are paying 41% more in monthly mortgage repayments than a decade ago, despite property prices remaining broadly stable in real terms. The average mortgage rate has risen from 1.72% in 2016 to 5.13% currently, adding £353 to monthly payments.

title: Corporate landlords plan expansion amid rental reforms
summary:
Corporate landlords with large property portfolios are continuing to plan business expansion six months after the Renters' Rights Act came into force, according to new research from LRG. The findings show 82% are actively planning to scale their businesses despite earlier concerns about the legislation.

title: UK housing sales outlook weakens to three-year low
summary:
The outlook for UK housing sales has deteriorated to its weakest level since July 2023, according to the latest RICS survey. Rising mortgage rates dampened buyer demand in October, with 12-month sales expectations falling to a net balance of -17%.

title: Chestertons joins relocation association as first agency
summary:
Chestertons has become the first estate agency to join the Association of Relocation Professionals, following 18 months of relationship building with the relocation industry. The membership positions the agency to work more closely with relocation management companies serving international employees moving to London.

title: London’s unsold high-end flats triple since 2016
summary:
The number of completed but unsold homes in central London has tripled since 2016, reaching 1,400 units by the end of September. New construction starts in zone 1 have fallen 75% over the past decade as developers face rising costs and weakened demand.
